races.name: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing "confined" Ebf Maiden Stakes (For Horses Which Have Run No More Than Once) (GBB Race)
Fine Details Car Valeting Sprint Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Utmost Respect
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer trained by Fahey, who fires at a big rate over the 14 days (9/60); won at 5f on good going in the form string and has fair course-and-distance profile, but the apprentice Tindall (5lb claim) is a useful offset in a big handicap field — needs to get a clean prominent pitch in a hectic early order.|
runners_data.comment: Utmost Respect showed a good level of form when winning five starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before, at a 136 lb burden from stall 12; the chief concern is that he has struggled to recapture that winning thread since.

runners_data.name: Kinnalargy
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old is a confirmed front-runner whose record on similar going reads nine runs without a win — form shows he gets involved early but hasn't converted; the key is whether Kevin Stott can establish lead authority with Managing Director also pressing — if he does, he's capable of lasting given the Ryan yard's current form.|
runners_data.comment: Kinnalargy has run over today's trip and going and our rating of 85 puts him third in a field of 21, marking him out as a leading contender; winless in his last five starts is the concern, though 44 days off may have him freshened for a bold bid from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with an excellent record at 5f on good ground (9/12 in similar going), and Joanna Mason brings significant course knowledge; travels to the line from off the pace and the handicap mark of 77 looks workable, but needs a gap to open in a 22-runner field — headgear-free now (blinkers on previously, shown as b).|
runners_data.comment: Call To Action arrives in fine fettle on 24 days' rest, with three runner-up finishes in his last four starts suggesting he is knocking on the door, and he has experience of today's distance and going; at 135 lb from stall six, however, a tough weight ask and a middling ranking in a 21-runner field are the checks against him.

runners_data.name: Sports Coach
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse from Antony Brittain's yard who has placed twice in similar going but never won on good turf — the record shows consistency without a killer finish, and in a race this congested Harry Russell will need to find daylight late that may not materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, Sports Coach has placed twice in that sequence and brings distance and going experience to this assignment, though 135 lb from stall 17 are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Explosive Finnish
runners_data.note: Kevin Frost's three-year-old is on a good trajectory — five in the form string reads 1-2-2-3, progression is clear, and the 6f win on good ground recently shows the yard has him in good order; prominent style suits this race shape ideally and Joe Leavy is a capable pilot for a horse whose confidence is building.|
runners_data.comment: Explosive Finnish won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but 44 days off the track raises a fitness query and 135 lb is a stern burden from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent type from Iain Jardine running with a hood (p), who recorded a win at 5f on good and two seconds at 5f on soft in recent outings — the return to good ground is the right surface and a 3lb claiming jockey, Nicholls, is an asset at the weights; competitive claims at OR 77.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed two and three starts back, and a winner five starts back, Parisiac returns in fair time off 16 days, but back-to-back disappointing efforts since — eighth most recently — are a concern at 135 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: True Promise
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for McSharry whose record on good going reads 0W/1P from four starts — the 135lb burden and inconsistent form string (including a 12th) make it hard to be enthusiastic about the chance in a field this competitive; Whiteley's 5lb claim helps, but the horse needs everything to fall right.|
runners_data.comment: True Promise has distance and going experience in his favour and a win four starts back gives his claims some substance, but seventh last time out and ninth two starts back make it hard to fancy him strongly from stall 16 off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse from Fahey whose last four runs all came at 6f — the drop back to 5½f at York is not obviously in his favour given the form, and though he has placed on good ground at 6f his recent string shows declining finishing positions; the 21-day gap is manageable.|

runners_data.name: Little Mi Mi
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's five-year-old prominent racer has won twice recently (OR 76) and arrives with real confidence — two wins at 5f on good ground in the last three starts, and Andrew Mullen is a solid booking; the pair are running in tandem with stablemate Parisiac which means splitting tactical decisions, but this one's form is more compelling.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our figures and drawn in stall 20, Little Mi Mi faces a stiff ask on these ratings despite showing a lively recent record that includes three wins in her last six starts, with a third last time out after back-to-back victories before that.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type from Katie Scott with an excellent record at 5f on good ground (11/15 sim-going, two wins); has been placed multiple times at this level without quite converting recently, and Jason Hart is a strong course jockey — needs clean passage but the profile is solid.|
runners_data.comment: Curious Rover won two starts back but has otherwise struggled for a top-three finish in recent starts, and 37 days off adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 134 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Duran
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing a visor (v) for Nigel Tinkler whose recent form is alarming — 0-0-0-5-11-16 in the last five — and the vee is presumably there to sharpen him up; recent runs at 5f on good going have produced double-digit finishes, and it is hard to construct a case for reversal here without a marked improvement.|
runners_data.comment: Duran's ratings profile stands out sharply in this field, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a winless recent sequence and a trainer who has drawn a blank in 22 attempts over the past fortnight make it hard to dismiss the stable's current slump as the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Vingegaard
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up runner with visor (v) from Paul Midgley whose single win at 6f on good ground earlier in the season was followed by a poor run; the going and distance are within range but the recent pattern is inconsistent and Ryan Sexton navigating 22 runners from the rear is a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well below most rivals on these figures, Vingegaard arrives on the back of an unplaced run and has won only once in his last six starts, making him hard to recommend, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and 39 days off may have freshened him.

runners_data.name: Copper Knight
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old veteran of Easterby's yard wearing a tongue-tie (t), sporting OR 74 — has placed three times on good ground but has never won at OR 74+ in recent history; David Allan is a smart jockey around York but the age and trajectory make it hard to place him ahead of younger, in-form alternatives despite the prominent style.|
runners_data.comment: Ninth last time out and unplaced the start before that, Copper Knight has struggled for consistency in recent starts, though a winner six starts back shows he retains ability; he has run over today's distance and going, and our rating of 83 offers some encouragement from stall one at 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald rides a confirmed front-runner for Geoff Oldroyd who won at 5f on good ground and has placed on similar going five times — the key is whether he can shake off Kinnalargy early; if he dictates, his record suggests he stays on well, and McDonald at York is a potent combination.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent recent form makes Managing Director the pick here — second last time out and a winner five starts back, he has experience of today's trip and conditions and steps in on a competitive mark of 74, though he will need to overcome stall 18 carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Roach Power
runners_data.note: Wigham's seven-year-old is a true hold-up horse whose natural race position is the rear, but the congestion of genuine hold-up types in this 22-runner field means he has been mapped to midfield — his best form at 5f comes from off the pace, and JF Egan is capable, but getting the right run here is genuinely uncertain.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 17th of 21 on our figures, Roach Power faces a stiff task from stall 22 carrying 131 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Kanishka
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type from Ian Williams whose last three runs were at 5f-6f on good ground but all finished 6th or worse — recent handicap form suggests the horse is struggling to find a gear change at these weights, and Cieren Fallon will need more than a clean trip to get involved.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Kanishka does arrive with distance and going experience to call on, but consecutive unplaced efforts are a concern; the 129 lb burden from stall nine adds further pressure on a gelding ranked towards the foot of this field.

runners_data.name: Bonnie's Boy
runners_data.note: Fahey's four-year-old naturally races from hold-up, but the volume of similar types in this field means he cannot guarantee his preferred late position — Oisin Orr brings class, and the horse has placed at 5f-6f on good going, but the redistribution into midfield means he races in a less comfortable position than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Bonnie's Boy has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out shows he retains some ability, but winless in his last five starts and carrying 129 lb from stall 19, this lightly tried gelding looks to have plenty working against him here.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old sprinter from Paul Midgley who holds a strong record at 5f on good and soft (nine runs, three places) but has not won at this level recently — Cam Hardie takes the ride, and while he is a genuine hold-up performer the sheer number of horses behind which he must carve a path in a 22-runner sprint tempers enthusiasm significantly.|

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old is a hold-up horse by inclination, bumped into midfield on the map by the weight of similar types — his best result in similar going was a second at 5f, and Paul Mulrennan is a shrewd jockey, but recent form (7-4-8 latest three) makes a bold assessment difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Oriental Prince has been winless in his last six starts, finishing no better than second two runs back and sixth most recently, and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, he is hard to fancy despite having experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's seven-year-old arrives in cracking form — two wins and a second in the last three starts, most recently just three days ago — and though naturally a hold-up horse in a crowded field, Rowan Scott is an experienced pilot; the rapid turnaround (3 days) is unusual but clearly the yard is confident, and the horse's in-form credentials are the strongest of the redistribution group.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and one of 21 runners to navigate from stall 21, Harb at least arrives in career-best form — a winner two starts back and again last time out — and has run over today's trip and going before, though the ratings gap makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Maharajas Express
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old has won at 5f on good ground twice in recent history and placed across a variety of surfaces — David Egan is a high-class booking — but as a natural hold-up horse mapped into midfield due to field congestion, securing the late run he needs will depend on luck in running that a 22-runner sprint rarely guarantees.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 19 of 21 on our figures and his speed rating lags well behind the top of this field, making Maharajas Express genuinely difficult to fancy, though a second last time out and a win three starts back show he retains some ability, and he has distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Tanjen
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent racer for Tim Easterby (who is firing — 12/80 over 14 days) with a recent 5f win on good ground and useful place strikes at the course-and-distance trip; Jake Dickson's 5lb claim helps at the weights and the prominent style is exactly what this race shape rewards — yard form is a strong positive.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Tanjen is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and an encouraging third last time out; she has run over today's trip and going before, but her speed rating leaves her with plenty to find on these weights.

races.paceDynamic: Kinnalargy and Managing Director are the two confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field, and both are likely to push for the early lead, creating a genuinely contested pace from the gates over 5½f on good ground at York. That rivalry between two genuine pace-setters means neither is likely to get an uncontested lead — both will be burning energy establishing position in the first furlong, setting an honest-to-brisk gallop that stretches the field. The prominent horses — Utmost Respect, Explosive Finnish, Little Mi Mi, Parisiac, and Copper Knight — will press them into a shape that generates enough tempo to suit horses who can settle just off the pace and finish with a clean run. This race shape most clearly favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can track the contested lead without overexerting and produce a sustained finish in the closing 2f; pure hold-up horses will need a lot to go right with 22 runners. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically race from the rear in a pack this large — Roach Power, Bonnie's Boy, Ventura Express, Oriental Prince, Harb, and Maharajas Express are all true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map, with Roach Power and Harb (in-form) most likely to find a viable position, but none can be certain of the clean passage they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Kinnalargy and Managing Director push each other along at a strong clip from the gates, the pace holds honest enough to reward the horse who travels prominently without fighting for position.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop between the two front-runners burns them off late, and a prominent horse who settles just behind the duelling leaders gets the perfect tow into the straight with energy in reserve; on good ground at York's 5½f the race is truly run and the finisher hitting the rising ground with momentum takes it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Poaches, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of Kinnalargy or Managing Director asserts dominance early and the other drops away, allowing the leader to control the tempo and dictate from the front.
scenarios.body: A controlled front-running display on good ground can be devastating over 5½f at York when the pace is metronomic rather than frantic; the leader preserves enough in the tank through the dip and finishes powerfully up the rise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace between the front-runners is truly fierce enough to set it up for horses slightly further back who can track through in a clear passage at the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: True hold-up horses redistributed into midfield — particularly Harb, who arrives in cracking form having won twice recently, and Call To Action — could benefit from an honest gallop creating gaps; this is viable but contingent on a clean run in a 22-runner sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle between Kinnalargy and Managing Director results in both folding, spreading the field wide and creating a muddling pace that yields a lottery finish.
scenarios.body: With 22 runners on a flat 5½f course and a chaotic early order, horses drawn and travelling advantageously in the middle of the field could steal the advantage as the field fans out in the straight; this is the lowest-probability shape because the going is good, not testing, reducing the chance of a full collapse.
