races.name: Hanson Springs Stayers Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Shadow Dance
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter, though OR 86 on this stiff York trip after a string of poor efforts on Soft; Rebecca Menzies yard at 1/17 over 14 days is modest, and her recent form (7-6700) does not inspire confidence beyond the pace role — style fit score of 0.93 flags she is being stretched positionally.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Shadow Dance nevertheless carries the strongest rating in the field and brings recent fitness — just 16 days since his last run — alongside experience of today's going, making him the one to side with despite a modest recent form line.

runners_data.name: Pinatique
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott yard in fine 14-day form at 6/19 and this 4yo will strip fitter on just its second run over staying trips; hold-up style has produced no wins or places on Good ground in six attempts, a genuine concern for a race likely dominated by prominent gallopers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pinatique nevertheless showed renewed promise with a fourth last time out after a couple of low-key efforts, and 22 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; carrying 142 lb against a competitive field may test her further, however.

runners_data.name: Percy Shelley
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with an outstanding Good-ground record (2W 10P from 14 runs) and two second places over 16f-20f at Good tracks; James Owen yard at 2/36 is quiet but this 7yo is a model of reliability at this type of trip and surface.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, Percy Shelley has been placed second three times in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 90 marking him a leading threat off 141 lb; the risk is he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Dual course and distance winner on Good ground, and visored today — headgear that has coincided with winning performances; shares a trainer with Percy Shelley and both arrive on a 31-day break in a yard that may not be firing at peak, but High Fibre's raw Good-ground stamina profile is the standout in this field.
runners_data.comment: High Fibre arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a clear threat at 141 lb; the concern is whether that weight blunts his momentum after a month off.

runners_data.name: Call My Bluff
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good ground six runs ago and showed a clean hold-up profile in that success; 91 days off is a long absence for a 9yo, and the parka headgear is retained, but the slow-tempo scenario is needed for this style to truly unlock.
runners_data.comment: Call My Bluff was a winner three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 90 marking him out as one of the strongest threats in the field; the main risk is a return from 91 days off.

runners_data.name: Rock N Roll Pinkie
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with five places from nine Good-ground runs, though no win at this distance band; De Sousa is a significant booking for this Ivan Furtado runner, and the recent Soft-ground form is modest — will need the field to open up in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Rock N Roll Pinkie arrives here 27 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and her second six starts back offers a hint of better ability — but she has been winless in her last six starts and her two most recent efforts, a seventh and ninth, leave her needing to find more.

runners_data.name: Moon Chime
runners_data.note: Two wins from six runs on Good ground including over 16f at this track — the most relevant course form in the field for a hold-up horse; hood retained, 50-day freshener could be positive, and this 8yo thrives when allowed to come from just off a strong gallop.
runners_data.comment: Moon Chime won last time out but faces a stiff test on a 50-day absence, and while he has run over today's trip before, his recent record beyond that win has been patchy, and carrying 131 lb against higher-rated rivals adds to the task.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from 10 Good-ground runs and placed third over 18f on Going Good just recently; Jim Goldie yard is in decent 14-day form at 3/29 and only 12 days since last run suggests fitness is sharp — parka headgear worn.
runners_data.comment: Trojan Sun has managed just one win in his last six starts, with a seventh and an unplaced run among those efforts making him hard to fancy ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, though he does return quickly fit on 12 days' rest and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Florida Dreams
runners_data.note: Recent form is sparse (only three runs shown) and shortest distance in recent history is 9f on Good — this 8yo is a natural hold-up type whose true style means it has been pushed into a midfield map position due to the volume of hold-up runners; 73 days since last run adds uncertainty, and the Good-ground record is thin at 0W 1P from two runs.
runners_data.comment: Florida Dreams has shown a placed effort in recent starts — third two runs back — but has been fifth on either side of it and is winless in that spell; 73 days off adds a fitness query, though his our rating of 76 suggests there may be more to find.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby yard in strong 14-day form (12/80) and this 7yo has three Good-ground places from 11 attempts; a natural hold-up horse that has been repositioned to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with rear-runners — the prominent horses ahead will likely dictate its fate.

runners_data.name: Marbuzet
runners_data.note: Won on Heavy ground and won on Heathcock, but the Good-ground record from 12 attempts shows only 0W though 7P — consistent but not a winner on this surface; another Easterby runner with the yard in form, and naturally a rear-runner who carries a redistribution to midfield because of the crowded hold-up group.
runners_data.comment: Marbuzet won last time out and returns on a quick seven-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but his overall recent form is patchy and he ranks ninth of twelve on our figures, making him hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Two wins from 10 Good-ground runs including over 14f and 16f — a genuinely versatile staying type; Jack Nicholls 3lb claim is an asset and the Iain Jardine yard is active (3/25 in 14 days) — blinkers headgear worn and 12 days since last run suggests readiness.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Newport is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back; he has been out of the frame on either side of that success, and while he has run over today's trip and going before and is fit enough at 12 days between runs, he faces a stiff task at these weights.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: Young 4yo stayer with improving form (4-3-2 in last three) on Good ground over 16-18f; Jim Goldie runner 12 days since last outing, and this natural hold-up type has been mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers — Lauren Young's 5lb claim softens the weight, and the horse is progressing through the ranks.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Furhaan is hard to fancy despite a recent run of placed efforts — he has run over today's trip and going before, and 12 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Dance is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field over 2m½f on Good ground at York, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate from the front at a measured, controlled tempo. Percy Shelley, High Fibre, Trojan Sun and Newport are all prominent-types who will press forward but none are natural pace-setters, meaning Shadow Dance should find a comfortable rhythm without being harried. The true hold-up horses — Florida Dreams, Gibside, Marbuzet and Furhaan — are so numerous relative to their natural positioning that several have been redistributed to midfield on the map; in practice, they are unlikely to secure the deep rear berths their style demands, and Florida Dreams and Marbuzet are the most likely to end up further forward than intended. A controlled, single-pace gallop on flat Good ground at York over this marathon trip strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain, with the premium on relentless galloping ability rather than a finishing kick — prominent racers and strong gallopers who avoid cover battles get the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shadow Dance Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Dance dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the field strings out before the home straight.
scenarios.body: Shadow Dance, racing without pressure, sets an even tempo that rewards those travelling prominently in her slipstream — the long York straight then becomes a sustained stamina test with no room for a sprint finish to materialise from deep. High Fibre and Percy Shelley, both proven on Good ground at this venue and trained by James Owen in strong form, are ideally placed to pounce off the pace without being far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Gallopers
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is too slow and the field bunches, creating a falsely-run race that compresses into a sprint-for-home up the straight.
scenarios.body: A crawl early over 2m½f can produce an unusually intense late dash where position in the final quarter-mile matters most, and horses who have travelled kindly without burning energy late-race come to the fore. Moon Chime and Marbuzet, both capable of landing a late challenge when the race is truly set up for sustained finishing, would benefit most from this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Percy Shelley, High Fibre and Trojan Sun all push for position early, raising the tempo and turning this into an honest, true-run staying contest.
scenarios.body: Increased pressure on Shadow Dance would raise the overall gallop, eliminating any false comfort and ensuring the race is decided by genuine stamina rather than a turn of foot — conditions that favour whoever travels most efficiently in a prominent berth. Newport and Trojan Sun, both proven over long distances on Good ground with strong trainer form, could thrive if rivals burn out ahead of them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely hot enough and the field spreads wide in the straight, giving hold-up horses a clear run through.
scenarios.body: This scenario relies on Florida Dreams, Gibside or Furhaan racing in their truest deep-set style and finding unobstructed passage — a less likely shape given how many are redistributed and likely to end up further forward than ideal. Call My Bluff, who won over 16f on Good ground and carries proven hold-up credentials, is the most credible beneficiary if this scenario against the race shape does materialise.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Dance's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the fulcrum of this race — if she is headed or pressured early by Percy Shelley or High Fibre pushing forward, the entire race shape changes and her chance of holding on evaporates.

High Fibre and Percy Shelley share a trainer (James Owen) and the same 31-day break — watch for any sign of market moves or jockey instructions that suggest one is being preferred, as both cannot win and one may be ridden as a pacemaker for the other.

Moon Chime's course-winning form over 16f on Good ground at York is the strongest hold-up credential in the field — if the early pace is genuinely strong, she could arrive late with a devastating run and her 50-day freshener may have her spot-on.

Florida Dreams, Gibside and Marbuzet are all true hold-up horses nudged into midfield on the map — watch in-running to see whether any of them actually drops away to the rear as instinct dictates, which would compromise their chance significantly if the gallop is steady.

Newport's blinkers and a 3lb claiming rider make this runner tactically unpredictable — if the Jardine team deploy him aggressively forward from a prominent position, he could inject unexpected pressure on Shadow Dance in the early stages of this 2m½f test.

races.name: Saltmoore Collection Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Noble Horizon
runners_data.note: Proven on Good ground with two wins over 10f in similar conditions, this hold-up specialist for Oli De Sousa benefits if the pace lifts; 16 days since last run is fine but needs the race to truly develop from the rear.

runners_data.name: Nesthorn
runners_data.note: Six consecutive placed finishes without a win, operating out of the top of the field, and 36 days off is a slight freshness unknown; hold-up style requires a strong gallop that this race may not supply given a lone front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked eighth of sixteen in the ratings, Nesthorn faces a stiff task, though a fourth two runs back offers a glimmer and 36 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; the 141 lb burden is no help.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: David Egan's mount has the style to push forward into a prominent position and is best suited by a proper pace over this trip; OR=93 but a tendency for wide-margin reversals (12th and 20th in recent runs) introduces variance.
runners_data.comment: Tuscan Hills steps back up having finished second last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and going — conditions that should suit his profile. Carrying 140 lb from stall 15, the trainer's current run of form is a reservation worth noting.

runners_data.name: Teumessias Fox
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who pulled up last time and has only one Good-ground placing in his last five runs over this sort of trip; the pace dynamic here does not set up well for a horse who needs strong fractions from deep.
runners_data.comment: Teumessias Fox has run over today's trip and going, our rating puts him narrowly top of this field, and 16 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, yet he is winless in his last five starts and that pulled-up effort is the main concern for backers.

runners_data.name: Have Secret
runners_data.note: Headgear notation (v = visor) adds a small unknown; the Fahey operation is firing (9 from 60 over 14 days) and this horse has winning form on Good over 10f, but recent form shows five finishes from 12th to 20th and he needs a thorough test.

runners_data.name: Let's Dream
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good ground and an established hold-up style with genuine finishing speed; Hector Crouch has experience with this five-year-old and the profile is solid, but a soft pace will blunt the late run this horse depends upon.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts give Let's Dream a solid recent foundation, but three modest efforts since suggest a return to form is needed; he has experience over today's trip and going, though 137 lb from stall 16 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Duke's Command
runners_data.note: Long absence of 115 days is the primary concern; David Tudhope's booking is positive but a genuine hold-up horse — his natural territory is the back of the field, not the midfield slot the map assigns him, so his chance is sensitive to whether the race tests stamina.
runners_data.comment: Duke's Command holds a strong profile on ratings and has run over today's trip and going, making him a clear danger — though winless in his last five starts and returning from 115 days off, questions over his current readiness are the main risk.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh partners this Fahey four-year-old who has shown genuine ability when prominent, placed four times in his last five starts; a hold-up type by nature compressed into midfield on this map, he needs racing room off the bend.
runners_data.comment: Castle Stuart shaped with some promise when third three starts back and second four starts back, but he is winless in his last six starts and a career-high 136 lb from stall 12 asks plenty of a colt who finished fifth last time out just 15 days ago.

runners_data.name: Besieged
runners_data.note: The unexposed three-year-old from Harry Charlton — three starts, progressive form of 2-2-1 — has the highest ceiling in the field; a prominent style on Good ground over 10f and the class upside make him a central figure in the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Besieged shaped with plenty of promise when winning last time out, but that run was 89 days ago and he ranks a distant thirteenth of sixteen on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights; he does at least have experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Dark Moon Rising
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves rides the seven-year-old Kevin Ryan veteran who wore hood last time (hg:p); a genuine hold-up horse placed on Good ground, but OR=87 and a recent pattern of middling finishes reduces confidence he can deliver from the compromised midfield map position.
runners_data.comment: Dark Moon Rising won two starts back but has since finished sixth, and while he has run over today's trip and going, his official mark of 87 and a mid-pack ranking among 16 runners suggest he faces a stiff ask to build on that victory from stall 2 off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Dhahabi
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old Ian Williams handler wearing tongue-tie (hg:t); form reads 0-0-0-0-0 in recent starts with sim-going positions averaging 12th out of 15, and his true hold-up style is further squeezed in this compressed field — very hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dhahabi does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and at 15 days since his last run he arrives fresh enough, though his record of late offers little encouragement from stall 11 under 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Empire Of Light
runners_data.note: Four wins in his last five starts on Good ground tells a compelling story; Grant Tuer's sprinter-turned-miler pushes forward from a prominent position and, with an 85-day break, freshness is untested but the recent record demands respect.
runners_data.comment: Empire Of Light has won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, but he was unplaced last time out, hasn't run in 85 days, and our figures rank him last of 16 here, making him very hard to recommend despite his experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old ran just seven days ago — the quick turnaround for a hold-up horse who found only moderate positions (4th, 4th, 3rd, 6th, 6th in recent runs) suggests he is in a rhythm but will need traffic luck given where he truly wants to race.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without threatening at the top, Wahdan has finished fourth, fourth, and third in his last three starts but remains winless in recent form; he has run over today's distance and going before, and a rating of 93 gives him claims, though 132 lb from stall eight is no soft task.

runners_data.name: Double Parked
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Tim Easterby's four-year-old has won over 10f on Good, wears tongue-tie (hg:t) and David Allan knows the horse — with no challenger for the lead he can control the tempo and simply has to be the central tactical figure.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 16 on our figures, Double Parked is hard to fancy after finishing unplaced last time out, and his sole recent victory came three starts back, with a third before it and a fifth since; distance and going experience at least counts for something.

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's four-year-old with blinkers (hg:b) has form over 10f on Good but is a true hold-up type filling a midfield map slot; four consecutive top-five finishes without a win signals consistency but limited upside, and 15 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15 of 16 on our figures, Wanderlust is hard to fancy despite the fitness edge of a 15-day turnaround and experience over today's trip and going; he carries 130 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old, ridden by Alec Voikhansky, has won over 10f on Good and pushed forward from a prominent position last time; an OR of 87 may understate ability and a clean run from a decent draw could see him feature prominently.
runners_data.comment: Pearl River won five starts back and shaped with promise when second four starts back, but he has failed to build on that in more recent outings, and a trainer striking at just 2% over the past fortnight is a significant concern heading into this.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Donny
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has four career placings from 10-12f trips on Good ground but is a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield; 58 days off means fitness is unproven and from OR=81 he needs career-best form to threaten here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14th of 16 on our figures, Stoneacre Donny faces a stiff ask, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and a second two starts back shows he retains some ability.

races.paceDynamic: Double Parked is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no credible challenger for the lead — Tuscan Hills, Besieged, Empire Of Light and Pearl River will push forward from prominent positions but none are natural pace-setters likely to take Double Parked on from the gate. With David Allan in the saddle and Tim Easterby's operation running hot (12 from 80 over 14 days), Double Parked can dictate a controlled, pressure-free gallop over a flat 1m2½f trip on Good ground, the ideal surface for his style. The field is unusually heavy with hold-up types — Duke's Command, Castle Stuart, Dhahabi, Wahdan, Wanderlust, Dark Moon Rising and Stoneacre Donny are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply insufficient space behind a single leader for every closer to get their natural berth; of these, Castle Stuart and Wahdan are best placed to at least edge into mid-division with cover. A solo leader controlling an unhurried, honest pace on flat Good ground at York — a track that rewards horses who travel prominently and have a turn of foot — clearly favours prominent racers and runners from the near side of midfield with finishing speed, not the deep closers who will need the pace to lift dramatically in the final quarter-mile, which Double Parked's likely tempo management will not guarantee.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Double Parked Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Double Parked is allowed to bowl along in front at a sustainable clip and the field fails to generate enough pace to string out the race.
scenarios.body: Double Parked sets a measured tempo through the long straight, kicks off the home turn, and the rail-hangers stalking just behind him get first run; horses from genuine hold-up positions have too much ground to make up against a moderate pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominents Pounce, Strong Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just quick enough that mid-division travellers can sustain their momentum into the final two furlongs without being stopped by a truly dawdled gallop.
scenarios.body: Horses tracking Double Parked just off the pace — Tuscan Hills, Besieged and Pearl River — move up smoothly off the bend and the sustained Good-ground gallop at 1m2½f allows a horse with class and recent fitness to collar the leader; the 3-year-old Besieged's unexposed profile at the trip gives him a strong appeal in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace lifts in the middle mile — perhaps Tuscan Hills or Empire Of Light applies pressure — and the race is run at a genuine clip that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A stronger tempo burns off Double Parked and the prominent horses, leaving the straighter stretches open for a closer travelling kindly in midfield; Noble Horizon and Let's Dream, both proven on Good ground and carrying strong sim-going records, are the logical threats from this group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Crowded, Late Drama
scenarios.trigger: If the 17-runner field produces significant trouble in running — bumping, blocking or a wide draw for prominent types — disrupting the expected orderly flow.
scenarios.body: With a large field and several hold-up types compressed into midfield out of role, the risk of traffic problems is real; any horse drawn favourably wide with a jockey willing to go early gets a clean passage while redistributed closers find themselves trapped.

watchPoints.text: Double Parked's early position is everything — if David Allan is forced wide at the break or if Tuscan Hills or Empire Of Light seriously challenges for the lead, the uncontested pace scenario collapses and Double Parked's chance is sharply reduced.

Besieged (Harry Charlton, unexposed 3yo) has shown a rapid progression across just three starts and is the highest-ceiling runner in the field — if he travels smoothly just off Double Parked, he could be a significant danger from the two-furlong pole.

Traffic risk is elevated in a 17-runner field where six-to-seven genuine hold-up types are compressed into midfield out of their natural role — watch for Castle Stuart and Wahdan in particular to find themselves blocked on the home bend.

Empire Of Light returns from an 85-day absence having won three on the bounce; Grant Tuer's horses can return fresh to win and if this horse has trained on, it is a major dark-horse threat from a prominent position.

The Fahey yard (Richard & Peter) runs two horses — Have Secret and Castle Stuart — and both jockeys (Orr and McHugh) will need to be aware of each other; stable tactics could influence how aggressively either is ridden in a crowded early-pace scenario.

races.name: Starman At Tally Ho Stud Garrowby Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Behike
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo with consecutive wins at 6f on Good and Soft, ridden by David Egan for the in-form George Scott yard; a natural forwardly-placed horse, though the volume of prominent types in this field means he cannot be guaranteed his ideal pitch and races with a positional discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Behike won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but ranked seventh of nine on our figures he faces a stiff ask at the top weight of 131 lb, and the recent unplaced effort in his last five starts tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Dickensian
runners_data.note: Shane Gray partners this Kevin Ryan-trained 3yo who has run exclusively over 5f in recent starts, so the step to 6f at York represents a genuine question mark; a hold-up horse with a strong Good-ground record (10 qualifying runs, 2 wins, 6 places), he needs the pace to be honest enough to bring his late effort into play.
runners_data.comment: Dickensian has run over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back shows he can find the winner's enclosure, but unplaced efforts either side of a seventh leave him needing to recapture that form off 131 lb from stall seven after 37 days away.

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner, trained by Andrew Balding and ridden by Shane Foley, with three wins from his last five at 6f on Good ground; his ability to control fractions unchallenged on a flat straight track is the defining structural feature of this race, and he is racing in his natural role.
runners_data.comment: Double Rush won three of his last five starts, with back-to-back victories two and three runs back giving him a potent winning thread, and he has experience of today's trip and going; the main concern is an eight-week absence since that disappointing eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Regional
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez rides this 8yo Edward Bethell stable runner who has 14 qualifying runs on similar going yielding 3 wins and 9 places — a model of consistency on Good turf; prominent style and proven course form over this trip make him ideally suited to tracking the pace in second or third and challenging late.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back shows Regional has ability at this level, and he returns on a going and trip he has experience of, carrying 130 lb from stall 8; winless in his last five starts, yet our rating of 119 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Spycatcher
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's 8yo was Listed-class over this course and distance earlier this season but has had a 106-day break and his Good-ground record (5 runs, no wins, no places) contrasts sharply with his all-weather and soft-ground form; Clifford Lee's mount needs to be at his sharpest on return and over a going surface that has not historically brought out his best.
runners_data.comment: Spycatcher won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories three and four starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the trainer is firing at 26% in the last fortnight, though a 106-day absence is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Extremely Zain
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly-raced 3yo, partnered by Cieren Fallon, steps back to 6f after winning over 7f and brings a strong recent profile (2 wins and 2 places from 4 similar-going runs); a prominent runner who can slot cleanly just behind the pace, his class edge and yard form make him a natural beneficiary of the controlled tempo Double Rush is expected to set.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into seventh last time out dampens the mood, but Extremely Zain has won three of his last five starts, with victories three, four, and five starts back, and he returns after 22 days with distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides this Richard Hughes 3yo filly who won over this course and distance and has 7 qualifying runs on Good ground (2 wins, 4 places); her tactical speed and proven 6f form at York make her a well-placed prominent runner, though she must overcome a slightly below-par effort last time when beaten into fourth.
runners_data.comment: America Queen arrives on the back of a win last time out, is unexposed over today's trip and going, and her 126 lb burden from stall one is the chief question mark against her.

runners_data.name: Nariko
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 5yo mare returns after a 302-day absence, which is the dominant concern here regardless of style considerations; she is by nature a front-running type who will struggle to secure her natural position in this prominent-heavy field, and the combination of layoff and positional compromise makes her profile difficult to support.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Nariko has been out of the frame in her last three starts, with an eighth last time out, and returns after a 302-day absence; two wins in her last five starts offer some hope, and she has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Lam Yai
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's 3yo, ridden by Sam James, has placed at 6f on Good and Soft but her last three runs have produced no wins and her form string tails off; like stablemate Spycatcher she is in a yard with 10 runners in 39 days which shows activity, but she is a naturally prominent horse whose preferred early position is taken by others in this field, meaning she may be farther back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Lam Yai faces a stiff ask, though she brings solid recent form — third, second, and a win in her last five starts — experience over today's trip and going, and a trainer striking at 26% in the past fortnight all count in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Double Rush is the confirmed front-runner and, with no other true lead horse in the field, is set to control the pace from the outset at York's straight six, dictating terms on Good ground at a measured, sustainable gallop. Extremely Zain, America Queen, and Regional are all prominent-style horses who will look to sit just behind Double Rush, creating a competitive but orderly early order rather than a blistering pace war. The field carries significantly more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Behike, Lam Yai, and Nariko are all natural prominent racers but are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield position once the prominent slots are filled by Double Rush, Extremely Zain, America Queen, and Regional; this is a structural advantage for those four and a positional compromise for the trio who cannot all claim their preferred pitch. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a comfortable, uncontested pace on a flat straight track — classically favours horses with tactical speed who can race prominently or close from a short distance, meaning prominent types and one-run hold-up horses with high cruising speeds are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Double Rush Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Double Rush is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the prominent pack behind him races into each other's pockets.
scenarios.body: Double Rush sets a measured pace, controls the fractions, and his rivals chase shadows before finding his lead too comfortable to reel in over the final two furlongs on good ground; prominent horses who can track him closely without wasting energy are the primary beneficiaries of a controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just quick enough to string the field out and a prominent tracker produces a decisive late run.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting two or three lengths off the leader picks up the gap left by a mildly-run race and finds enough to collar Double Rush close home; Regional's proven course form and America Queen's recent winning burst make them the logical candidates in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally faster than expected and the late runners find a clear run through a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: Spycatcher or Dickensian, both genuine hold-up types, would need to find a gap off a genuinely pressured gallop; Spycatcher's five-month break is a concern but his Going record at this course and distance is the main credential, while Dickensian's proven Good-ground form over 5f makes the step to 6f here the key unknown.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Plays Havoc
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types press Double Rush harder than expected, fracturing the pack and producing a messy, inconclusive pace picture.
scenarios.body: Behike, Lam Yai, or Nariko force their way closer than their redistributed mapping suggests, burning early energy across the field and creating a rough race in which the cleanest traveller benefits; this is the least likely shape given only one confirmed pace-setter exists, but a positional scramble among the prominent glut could disrupt even the front pair.

watchPoints.text: Double Rush (Foley/Balding) is the sole confirmed front-runner and if he lands a clean break from the stalls he may never be headed — watch for his opening two furlongs to see whether any prominent horse contests his lead.

The cluster of prominent types — Extremely Zain, America Queen, Regional, Behike, Lam Yai, and Nariko — means early positional jostling could be significant; if three or more of them push forward simultaneously, the pace dynamic shifts from controlled to pressured and the race shape changes materially.

Spycatcher's 106-day absence is the longest in the field and his Good-ground turf record (0 wins, 0 places from 5 runs) is a red flag for the surface; watch his market moves in the final hour for any confidence signal from the Burke yard.

Nariko's 302-day layoff makes her the biggest fitness unknown in the race — even if she recovers her prominent style, that volume of time off over a trip at Listed level warrants close scrutiny before any assessment of her chances is made.

Regional's age (8) and his exceptional Good-ground record (14 runs, 3W 9P) make him a reliable barometer of how the pace is developing — if he travels sweetly into the final two furlongs, a fast-finishing hold-up horse will need to be exceptional to get past him.

races.name: Eboracum Security Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: He's A Monster
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse returning from 378 days off — the layoff is a significant flag — but his only win and place on similar going came in softer form, and George Wood will need to find daylight late in a congested finish; freshness could be a positive or a negative at this trip.
runners_data.comment: He's A Monster arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, with a speed rating of 95 underlining his claims; the concern is a layoff of 378 days, which leaves his fitness on trust.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who thrives on Good ground with 14 from 15 runs on similar conditions, Connor Beasley knows him well, and his prominent style is a natural fit for sitting just off Power Fizz — headgear (p) suits a horse that needs to travel positively, and he won over 7f Good last time comparable enough to matter.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out following a win the start before, Northern Express brings strong recent form to this assignment, has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 106 puts him clear at the top of this 15-runner field; 36 days between runs is the only minor query.

runners_data.name: Bobby Bennu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's five-year-old wears headgear (h) suggesting he can be keen, which is a concern in a prominent battle for position; his Good-ground record is modest (9 from 15) and Robbie Downey will need to find a clean passage from what could be a hectic early phase.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bobby Bennu nonetheless shaped with promise when second one start back, and having run over today's trip and going before, he arrives carrying 141 lb from stall seven with fitness intact after 39 days; the risk is he has yet to convert that placed effort into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Power Fizz
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field; Cieren Fallon for William Haggas is a potent combination, and two wins over 7f Good give this horse legitimate claims if allowed to roll along uncontested — the concern is whether he truly stays in front when pace picks up two out.
runners_data.comment: Power Fizz won two of his last five starts, including a victory three starts back, but has been unplaced in his two most recent outings; he has run over today's trip and going, though 141 lb from stall 11 makes life no easier as he bids to rediscover that form.

runners_data.name: Houquetot
runners_data.note: Harry Davies takes the ride on a hold-up type whose form string shows he tends to plug on rather than quicken sharply — Good-going figures are modest (5 from 10, no wins), and a 64-day break means fitness cannot be assumed; likely to be a minor player at best.
runners_data.comment: Houquetot has run over today's trip and going before and, with our rating of 98 lending him strong claims against this field, he shapes as a genuine danger from stall ten carrying 139 lb; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Great Dream
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's four-year-old has no wins on Good ground from three attempts (0 from 11 on sim-going) yet does want to race prominently — headgear (p) indicates he needs to be on the bridle early, and Dale Swift must use him to secure position without burning him in the battle for spots behind Power Fizz.
runners_data.comment: Great Dream won one start back but has since disappointed, finishing seventh last time out, and while he has experience over today's trip and conditions, 138 lb from stall 14 makes life harder for a gelding ranked mid-field on ratings.

runners_data.name: Khafiz
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's hold-up type has form figures of 4-4-12-11-25 at the sort of distances and going this represents — Kevin Stott will need a clean run and likely a strong pace to be delivered late, conditions that are not guaranteed today.
runners_data.comment: Khafiz is yet to win in his last six starts, though back-to-back fourth-place finishes one and two runs back show he can get competitive, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the 136 lb burden is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: A three-year-old who has won twice on Good over 7f and whose hold-up style (headgear: ht) means Kaiya Fraser must find a gap from behind — Stuart Williams has four winners from 29 runners in 14 days, giving the yard good momentum, and if the traffic parts this could run on well.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 15 on our figures, Utmost Good Faith has been unplaced in his last two starts and carries a hefty 135 lb from stall nine, making him hard to fancy; his sole win in recent starts came immediately before that pair, and experience over today's trip and going is about the best that can be said for him.

runners_data.name: Humam
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's four-year-old is a true hold-up horse positioned in midfield on the map only because the rear is overcrowded; Callum Rodriguez will face the same traffic hazards as the other closers, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 this runner is unlikely to reproduce its best when squeezed out of its natural rhythm — headgear (t) and a 22-day return are neutral.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11 of 15 on our figures, Humam faces a stiff ask from stall 12 carrying 135 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a third one start back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mr Noble
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke has had 10 winners from 39 runners in the past 14 days — excellent yard form — and this three-year-old has five consecutive placed or winning runs in the last six starts; Clifford Lee can use his prominent style to sit close to Power Fizz, and the 10-day turnaround suggests he is primed.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and shaped well when second the start before, but he drops to eighth in a field of fifteen on our rating and that speed figure of 81 is a mild concern; the trainer's 26% strike rate over the past fortnight keeps him firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who won last time on Good over 7f but is mapped to midfield because the rear is full — Warren Fentiman (claim) rides, and the STYLE_FIT flag means his chance is discounted if he cannot replicate his natural pattern; the visor (v) is retained from the win so headgear is consistent.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has been unplaced in both outings since, and that patchy recent form is the concern; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 36 days fresh off a break could spark a revival from stall two carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: U Sure Do
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has three wins from 15 on Good-type going (10 from 15 similar-going runs), wears headgear (t) for concentration, and Jake Dickson (5lb claim) rides; U Sure Do wants to race prominently but will have to fight hard for that ground in a congested early phase.
runners_data.comment: Won earlier in the campaign but has been well held in both runs since, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, 130 lb from stall 15 makes life harder for a horse who needs to rediscover that winning form.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Six consecutive seconds is one of the form stories of the race — Jim Goldie's five-year-old finishes reliably but seemingly cannot win; Lauren Young (5lb claim) rides, this is a true hold-up type redistributed onto the map for space, and while the placings are admirable the lack of a finishing kick to win is a structural concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts — all six resulting in second — Woohoo is hard to fancy ranked bottom of the field on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns after just 17 days off the mark.

runners_data.name: First Time
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's three-year-old has placed in three of the last five over 7f Good and Barry McHugh knows the track; a prominent style and consistent form on this going (9 from 10 similar-going runs) make this a runner to respect on a pace-fits-all basis, if position can be secured.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 12 of 15 on our figures, First Time is hard to fancy here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and does emerge placed third on two occasions in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Quest For Fun
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old prominent type who is genuinely displaced to midfield because there are simply too many horses for that berth; David Allan rides and Tim Easterby has strong numbers this fortnight, but the STYLE_FIT tag and a 44-day break since last run mean this veteran faces an uphill task if unable to get close to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 13 of 15 on our figures, Quest For Fun faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a couple of recent thirds offer slim encouragement, but the overall profile makes him hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Power Fizz is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Cieren Fallon can dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop over York's 7f. Behind him, a congested cluster of prominent-seeking horses — Northern Express, Bobby Bennu, Great Dream, Mr Noble, U Sure Do, and First Time — will fight hard for the best positions between the first and second furlongs, creating significant traffic interference two to three out. Quest For Fun, Humam, Our Havana, and Woohoo are genuine hold-up or prominent types redistributed on the map because they cannot all secure their natural position in a field this deep and wide; of those, Northern Express, Mr Noble, and Great Dream are best placed to actually punch through into prominent ground, while Quest For Fun and Our Havana are most likely to find themselves further back than ideal. The race shape — a controlled pace set by one horse, with the mid-section bunched and traffic-laden — strongly favours well-placed prominent racers who can sit just off Power Fizz without getting buried, rather than hold-up horses who must weave through a wall of runners late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Power Fizz Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Power Fizz is allowed to roll along unchallenged and the prominent horses behind him travel smoothly through the first four furlongs.
scenarios.body: Fallon dictates a measured tempo and the field strings out in an orderly fashion, giving the best-placed prominent horses a clean run into the straight; as the pace lifts approaching the two-furlong pole, those sitting two to three lengths off the leader have first crack at a potentially beatable front-runner. Prominent types with Good-going profiles and course fitness benefit most from this controlled, draughtsman's pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle for position in the first two furlongs creates a messy, stop-start tempo and those wide in the straight are gifted daylight.
scenarios.body: The scrimmaging among Northern Express, Bobby Bennu, Great Dream, U Sure Do, and First Time produces uneven fractions, and any runner caught in the melee burns energy; a horse that drops out of the battle early and finds a clear path down the outside in the final two furlongs can benefit as rivals tire. Hold-up horses who genuinely settle — He's A Monster and Utmost Good Faith — are the logical beneficiaries if the pace is genuinely honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Front Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble creates gaps and interference, allowing Power Fizz to steal an uncontested break while rivals check each other.
scenarios.body: Fallon, sensing chaos behind, quickens through the final three furlongs before the pack organises itself; Power Fizz's strong York form and Good-going record give it legitimate claims to hold on if the gap is significant enough. The prominent horses most likely to bridge the gap are those quickest to disengage from the mid-pack tangle — Mr Noble and Great Dream, both with tactical pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Slot In, Cause Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Quest For Fun, Our Havana, or Woohoo beat the map and secure closer positions than expected, altering the race shape.
scenarios.body: This requires one of the redistributed runners to break sharply and take a prominent berth that another horse concedes, fundamentally changing the competitive picture; in practice STYLE_FIT penalties and field size make this unlikely, but Woohoo's consistent placed form and Our Havana's recent win on Good give them residual upset claims. The probability is discounted materially because these runners are not genuine holders of their mapped positions.

watchPoints.text: Power Fizz (Cieren Fallon) is the lone front-runner — watch whether he is allowed a truly uncontested lead or whether Northern Express or Mr Noble push up to challenge him within the first two furlongs, as that single variable determines the entire race shape.

The prominent battle between Northern Express, Bobby Bennu, Great Dream, Mr Noble, U Sure Do, and First Time for the four or five positions immediately behind Power Fizz will create serious interference two to three furlongs out — any runner caught wide or checked at that point is effectively out of the race.

He's A Monster is returning from 378 days off — watch his market moves closely, as significant support would suggest home confidence despite the layoff, while a drifting price confirms a lack of fitness confidence from the yard.

Woohoo's six consecutive runner-up finishes mean she is statistically overdue to either win or capitulate — watch whether she is able to get closer in running than normal, which would be the signal she has found a gear that has previously eluded her.

Quest For Fun, Our Havana, and Humam are all tagged as runners racing out of their preferred role today — if any of them break sharply and secure prominent ground at the start, reassess their chances immediately as they become materially more dangerous than their redistributed map position implies.

races.name: Coopers Marquees Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Master Richard
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in an 19-runner field; trainer Ann Duffield has just one run in the past 14 days suggesting a measured approach, and his similar-going record of just 1W from 9 runs at this trip warrants scrutiny, but he controls the race from flag to finish and draws maximum benefit from an uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Master Richard has placed four times in his last five starts but remains winless, and while he has run over today's trip and going, that ninth last time out clouds his claims; the 142 lb burden from stall 13 does little to ease the task.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is firing (10/39 in 14 days) and this horse arrives on the back of winning two of his last four starts over 8f on Good ground — an ideal profile; tracking the leader from a prominent pitch, his form reads better than his OR of 80 suggests.
runners_data.comment: Inspired arrives on the back of a win last time out and has been consistently competitive in recent starts, with a second two starts back to go with that latest success; he has experience of today's distance and going, though 142 lb from stall 10 is no gimme for a gelding rated 80.

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: Consistent in the frame on Good over this distance but winless from his last five outings; 35 days off means Ellison brings him fresh, though with so many prominent types in this field he may be forced wider than ideal and that outside berth could cost him ground on York's straight track.
runners_data.comment: Ranked highest of the 19 runners on our rating and boasting distance and going experience, Lir Speciale is a genuine threat off an official mark of 84, returning fresh after 35 days; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts and must reverse a run of declining figures.

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Five of his last six runs have been placed (1W, 6P) on Good ground over 7-8f, making him one of the most reliable profile fits in the field; blinkers fitted, which often sharpens his early engagement, and Roger Fell's yard has two winners from 14 runs in the past fortnight — a genuine threat from a prominent draw.
runners_data.comment: Alpha Capture arrives in fine nick, placed five times in his last six starts including second last time out, and has experience of both today's trip and going; the concern is whether he can convert that consistency into a win, with just the one victory in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: Two wins from 11 runs on Good ground and a win over this course and distance in recent form; tongue-strap fitted, returns after 15 days and holds up off a strong pace — the most credible hold-up beneficiary if the race quickens sharply late and gaps open down the York straight.
runners_data.comment: Rajapour won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but he ranks 14th of 19 on our figures, with a speed rating well below the top end of this field, and 141 lb from stall 18 makes this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Proud Nation
runners_data.note: Won over 7f Good ground and has course experience, but the step back to a mile after a softer-ground run is a slight question mark; Fahey's yard is active and well-stocked, though at OR 86 he is one of the top weights in the apprentice race and must overcome the prominent congestion to finish on the premises.
runners_data.comment: Proud Nation shaped with real promise when second two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going reads well for a bold show here; the main concern is that he was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: King Casper
runners_data.note: Recent form figures of 0-9-0-8 tell a concerning story on Good ground; Brittain has just one winner from 10 runners over the past two weeks, and with King Casper repeatedly well beaten over this trip on similar ground, this looks a tough assignment at OR 81.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, King Casper hasn't threatened recently, though he has run over today's distance and going before and our rating edges above his official mark — modest claims from stall five carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Landed a win over this distance and surface 26 days ago (1/8f/Good), making him a live contender fresh off a career-best effort; tongue-piece fitted and prominent style suits the expected race shape, though Jim Goldie's yard has been modestly active and his price of OR 79 leaves margin for error.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Dwindling Funds is hard to fancy after finishing ninth last time out, and though he has experience over today's trip and going, that 136 lb burden makes life even harder.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is operating at volume (12/80 in 14 days) which can dilute individual focus; Son has been placed without winning over this trip on Good ground, and with tongue-piece fitted and prominent style he will be in the scrimmage for position — consistency without a win is the recurring theme.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Son has posted a third last time out and a second two starts back to show he's knocking on the door, but the 136 lb burden and draw 16 are notable factors; experience over today's trip and going at least leaves him with no unknown quantities.

runners_data.name: Melvin Udall
runners_data.note: 66 days off is a notable absence and his last win came on Soft ground, raising a gentle query about whether Good suits at this level; headgear includes a hood, and while he won at OR 78, the long lay-off combined with a lack of Good-ground winning form leaves him needing to prove fitness on return.
runners_data.comment: Melvin Udall won four starts back but has been out of the placings in his three most recent outings, and a 66-day absence adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 135 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old from Easterby's busy operation; her last run at 2/8f/Good is the standout piece of form in a string otherwise dominated by poor efforts, and as a hold-up type she will need a truly run race and clean passage to get competitive — the best of the hold-up prospects if things fall right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Daydreama at least boasts a second two starts back to suggest ability, though an unplaced effort last time out and a hefty 135 lb to carry from stall 19 are the hurdles he faces here, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Advance Twentyfive
runners_data.note: Won over 8f Good 22 days ago (OR 82, similar trip) and wears a visor for focus; hold-up style means he needs to navigate the traffic that will build through the final quarter-mile, and his trainer Fahey's dual entries in this race (with Proud Nation) could complicate tactical decisions.
runners_data.comment: Advance Twentyfive arrives here 22 days on from a winning effort two starts back, and with experience of both today's trip and going, conditions pose no unknown quantities; the ninth last time out is the one note of caution, but the profile still makes him an appealing pick at 134 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Callisto Dream
runners_data.note: Won last time out at Southwell over 8f on soft going, returning after 107 days off; by nature a prominent racer, he has been pushed back to a midfield mapping because the field is saturated with prominent types, and his chance is tempered by the likelihood he cannot secure his preferred berth in such a compressed field.
runners_data.comment: Callisto Dream has run over today's trip and going, and did win last time out, but 107 days off the track is a concern and she ranks sixteenth of nineteen on our figures, making her very hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old who won over this course and distance (1/8f/Good) in recent form — a directly relevant piece of evidence; hold-up style ridden by a 7lb claimer could be a compound advantage if Molly Keegan-Price can pilot her through gaps in the straight, and 29 days between runs is a conventional prep.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, Illy's Roo is hard to fancy despite a reasonable 29-day break, with five unplaced efforts dominating recent starts; his one win in that sequence came three starts back, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Be Frank
runners_data.note: Has been consistent without winning in recent starts, all on varying going; a genuine hold-up horse in terms of style, he has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, but his true pattern is to be produced late — the redistribution means he may race closer than usual, which is not his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 17th of 19 on our figures, Be Frank has shown little encouragement in recent outings, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns with 86 days between runs potentially freshening him up.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: OR 72 and a going preference flag (headgear: p); Scott Dixon's yard has no winners from 24 runs in the past 14 days, which is a significant training-form concern, and Canvas has finished outside the top six in five of his last six starts on Good ground — limited profile at this level.
runners_data.comment: Canvas is winless in his last five starts and he races from a trainer who has yet to land a winner in the past 14 days, though experience over today's trip and going, a return after 22 days, and a rating of 81 offer some encouragement for this midfield contender.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: Won over 8f Good at OR 75 and placed multiple times over this distance; a 3-year-old wearing a hood, he will track through the hold-up group and needs the race to develop into a late sprint — Mark Walford's modest recent form (1/15) slightly tempers the appeal of an otherwise solid individual profile.
runners_data.comment: Substance was third three starts back and runner-up last time out, but the sixth two starts back highlights some inconsistency; carrying 127 lb from stall 6, he has experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 81 gives him a fighting chance.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: A veteran at OR 68 who has placed relentlessly without winning (0W from his last seven starts on Good); a genuine hold-up type who has been pressed into a midfield position by the volume of rear-held horses in this field — Easterby's busy operation and his pattern of near-misses suggest a place rather than a win is the likely ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of near-misses giving way to back-to-back fourths, Barley finds himself ranked 18 of 19 on our figures and looks hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Empirestateofmind
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old at OR 67 with modest recent form, returning after 43 days; blinkers and a hold-up style define him, but he too has been repositioned to midfield because the rear is congested — his age, modest going-specific record and trainer's moderate 14-day figures (3/14) make him one of the hardest to enthuse about here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and unplaced last time out, Empirestateofmind heads here 43 days later with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour, though a mark of 67 and a midfield ranking suggest he faces a stiff task returning to form.

races.paceDynamic: Master Richard is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse wanting to lead, he can dictate his own fractions down the York straight mile without being pressured into a suicidal gallop — a fundamentally sustainable pace shape. Behind him, a significant cluster of prominent-position horses — Inspired, Lir Speciale, Alpha Capture, Proud Nation, Son, Dwindling Funds, King Casper and Melvin Udall — will compress into the chasing group from the outset, creating a scrimmage for the best berths from two to three furlongs out that will produce significant traffic issues for those unable to find daylight early. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Inspired and Alpha Capture, both with recent course or trip form and in-form connections, are best placed to win the battle for the rail behind Master Richard, while Lir Speciale, Son and Proud Nation will be squeezed further back than ideal. The race shape strongly favours a prominent racer that can track Master Richard's honest but uncontested pace and produce a clean turn of foot from two furlongs out, before the hold-up brigade can navigate the inevitable traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Master Richard sets a steady, uncontested pace and a prominent horse travels smoothly into second or third position throughout.
scenarios.body: Master Richard's lone lead will set an honest but manageable tempo, allowing a well-placed prominent rival to stalk him comfortably and kick clear once the race ignites over the final two furlongs; the York straight favours horses with a fluent rhythm rather than those forced wide or into tight gaps.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Master Richard dictates an unusually slow early gallop and steals a decisive advantage that the field fails to reel in.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to take him on from the front, Master Richard could build a substantial lead that becomes race-winning as the prominent pack burns energy scrimmaging behind; his rider Alexandra Egan's ability to judge pace becomes the critical factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and creates a genuine sprint finish that rewards those held up for a late run.
scenarios.body: Rajapour or Daydreama, held off the pace and avoiding the prominent congestion, could find clear daylight in the final furlong if the front group ties up; Rajapour's recent winning form over course and distance on Good ground makes him the most credible beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cavalry charge creates a wall of horses two furlongs out and a redistributed or mid-division runner finds an unlikely gap.
scenarios.body: Callisto Dream and Barley, though mapped out of their natural positions due to field congestion, could benefit from a chaotic finish where conventional traffic patterns break down; however, both carry a style-fit discount and this scenario depends on a degree of disorder rather than clean racing.

watchPoints.text: Master Richard (Alexandra Egan) sets the only confirmed pace in a 19-runner field — watch for him to control the fractions entirely unchallenged, because if he steals four or five lengths on a slow early clip the prominent pack will have to commit energy to close, fundamentally reshaping who wins.

The eight prominent-style horses — Inspired, Lir Speciale, Alpha Capture, Proud Nation, Son, Dwindling Funds, King Casper and Melvin Udall — will create a wall of horses chasing Master Richard from flag to two furlongs out; watch for significant bumping, checking and traffic carnage between the two and three furlong markers as they compress.

Rajapour (Conor Whiteley) is the most credible hold-up threat but will need a seam to open down the York straight; watch whether the prominent congestion actually clears in time — if it does not, he may never get a clean run despite having the form to win.

Callisto Dream (107 days off, true prominent type mapped to midfield) — watch for a sluggish or uncharacteristic start that reflects the layoff combined with racing out of his preferred position; if he fires fresh despite the break, the redistribution note becomes less relevant and he re-enters calculations quickly.

Apprentice jockeys dominate the saddle throughout this field — watch for inexperienced positional decisions in the early stages, particularly around the one-mile start at York where gaps form and close quickly; a rider error from any of the 3lb or 7lb claimers in the prominent pack could trigger a chain reaction of interference.
